_about: Size budget for the shipped payload (#669).
These limits are a ratchet, exactly like the coverage thresholds in
vite.config.js: they sit just above the numbers as they stand today so a
change that makes the app materially heavier fails loudly, and they are
meant to be raised deliberately — in the PR that grows the payload, with
the before/after in the commit message — rather than nudged up to get a
red run green.
Raising a limit is a normal thing to do. Doing it in a commit that says
nothing about why the payload grew is not: the number is the record.
Measured by scripts/size-summary.mjs against dist/ after `npm run build`.
All limits are gzipped bytes, because that is what crosses the network.
Baseline on main @ 60e38b6 (2026-09-08):
entryJs   83643 B    entryCss   4371 B    vocab  1148952 B
Raised for the slipped / at-risk inspection work: the recovery model, the
status-card component and the word card's recovery panel add 1809 B of
entry JS (85848 -> 87657) and 277 B of entry CSS (4393 -> 4670), the
latter after moving the shared word-row rules out of two scoped copies
into src/style.css. Both limits move back to roughly the 2 KB / 200 B of
headroom they were set with.
Raised again for the spaced-review work: the due-first ordering in
lib/sessionPools.js, lib/reviewState.js and the word card's review panel
add 1415 B of entry JS (87762 -> 89177) and 129 B of entry CSS
(4695 -> 4824). Both limits move back to the same 2 KB / 200 B
of headroom; without the raise entry JS would sit at 99.4% of budget and
the next one-line change would fail the build.
Vite 8 remeasurement (no limit change): Vite 8 splits what Vite 6 emitted
as a single entry chunk, and the pieces are modulepreloaded from
index.html rather than script-tagged. size-summary.mjs counted only the
script tag, so entryJs appeared to fall 87.9 -> 28.2 KiB while the bytes a
launch downloads barely moved. It now counts the preloaded chunks too, and
the comparable figure is 85.4 KiB — 2.5 KiB *below* the Vite 6 number, so
the limit stays at 91200 B and keeps its headroom.
Raised for the bomb-disposal minigame (#728). The game itself is a lazy
route chunk and costs the entry nothing; what lands in the entry is
`voiceAvailable` in lib/speech.js, the new route and the extra drill-list
entry — together 89266 -> 89938 B, about 670 B. Without the raise the entry
would sit at 98.6% of budget and the next one-line change would fail the
build, so the limit moves 91200 -> 92000 B, restoring the ~2 KB of headroom
the number is set with.
Raised again for HomeView's Minigames section (#726/#728): the card, its
game rows and their icons take entry CSS 4845 -> 4910 B, about 65 B, which
left only 120 B under the old 5030 B limit — below the ~200 B this number
is set with — so it moves 5030 -> 5150 B. Entry JS moves 89940 -> 90116 B
with the list and its markup, and stays inside the limit raised above.
Raised for the firewatch minigame (#731). Like bomb disposal it is a lazy
route chunk — the simulation, the canvas renderer and the numeral parser
all land there — so what reaches the entry is only the new route and the
extra Minigames row: 90116 -> 90256 B, about 140 B. That left 1744 B under
the 92000 B limit, below the ~2 KB this number is set with, so it moves
92000 -> 92300 B. Entry CSS is unchanged at 4908 B: the game's styles are
scoped to the lazy view.
Raised for the meaning-maze minigame (#752), the third game to do this. It
is a lazy route chunk and its scoped CSS rides with it, so entry CSS does
not move; what reaches the entry is the new route and the extra Minigames
row — 91518 -> 91865 B, about 350 B, measured against main at the firewatch
merge. That leaves 435 B under the 92300 B limit, so it moves 92300 ->
93900 B for the ~2 KB of headroom the number is set with.
Three raises in three games, all of them the same ~150-350 B of route and
list entry, is the shape to watch: the games are lazy and cost the entry
almost nothing each, but the entry itself has grown ~1.6 KB since #728
from work elsewhere, which is what keeps eating the headroom.
Inflection crush (#751) is the fourth game and the first not to need a
raise: the same shape of cost — a lazy route chunk, scoped CSS riding with
it, and only the route and the Minigames row reaching the entry — 91862 ->
92001 B, about 139 B, measured against main at the meaning-maze merge. That
leaves 1899 B under the 93900 B above, which is the ~2 KB this number is
set with, so the limit is left alone deliberately: the headroom the previous
raise bought is there to be spent, and moving the number for every game
would make it a rubber stamp rather than a ratchet.

entryJs.label: Entry JS (gzip)
entryJs.why: The bundle every launch pays for before anything renders. Vue, the router, the stores and the lib engine accumulate here; route chunks are lazy and deliberately excluded, so a route module pulled into the entry by a stray top-level import shows up as growth here.

entryCss.label: Entry CSS (gzip)
entryCss.why: The render-blocking stylesheet, for the same reason.

vocab.label: Vocab payload (gzip)
vocab.why: Every dist/vocab/*.json a first install downloads. It only ever grows, and nouns.json is roughly half of it. Build-time derived data (#657) legitimately moves work into this number — that is the trade being made, so raise the limit there and say by how much.
